messages:
Nina K: Hey team — heads up I'm planning parental leave starting 2026-06-01. Quick Qs: can I stack my remaining PTO the week before so it's paid? Does that change how our 401(k) match gets applied? Also thinking about a possible part-time (0.6 FTE) return — how would that affect benefits eligibility/coverage? Finally, who should I coordinate laptop return with and when? cc @people-ops @payroll
Sarah (People Ops): Congrats! :tada: Short answers: yes you can use PTO before leave (PTO is regular pay). 401(k) employee deferrals happen on paychecks, employer match is per-pay-period so it only applies when deferrals are taken. We'll loop in payroll to confirm paycheck dates so you know which pay periods will include a match. Part-time returns can affect eligibility if you drop below the benefits-hours threshold (typically 30 hrs/wk) — we need to check your planned schedule. For equipment: keep the laptop until your last active workday unless you want to ship earlier; EngOps handles pickup/shipping.
Payroll Bot: Automated note — payroll processes employee deferrals on the pay period when the earnings are recorded. If you convert PTO to unpaid leave, deferrals will stop and matches only occur for pay periods with deferrals. For precise dates, email payroll@redwood.com with your employee ID.
Marcus - EngOps: We can do a pickup or send a pre-paid return label. Ping me ~2 weeks before your last office day and we'll schedule. If you prefer to keep gear while on leave for continuity, that's fine — just inventory it with EngOps.
Nina K: Thanks — that helps. If I formally switch to 0.6 FTE on return, do I need to re-enroll in benefits or is it automatic? Any blackout windows I should worry about?
Sarah (People Ops): You usually don't need to re-enroll immediately; changes to coverage happen during the benefits update process after status change. However premium shares and company contributions can change based on FTE. There are enrollment windows for some add-ons. Also: if you're claiming short-term disability (STD) for birth recovery, submit the STD paperwork before your leave start so benefits can be coordinated. We'll send an estimator for costs after the FTE change.
Anish (Legal): If you're based in the UK (or other non-US region), statutory pay rules differ and payroll/legal will calculate differently. For US FMLA protections, make sure dates are precise on the leave form so job-protection metrics are accurate. Happy to review specifics via DM.
Sarah (People Ops): Action items for Nina: 1) Submit the leave request form: https://hr.redwood/leave-form (check the "use PTO before leave" box) 2) Email payroll@redwood.com with your desired PTO pay dates and employee ID so they can map match/paycheck timing 3) Ping @Marcus - EngOps ~2 weeks before last workday for equipment pickup/shipping 4) I'll schedule a 15-min benefits call to walk through part-time scenarios.
Nina K: Awesome, doing that now. Thanks everyone.
HR Bot: Leave request created — ID LR-2026-4587. Sarah (People Ops) has been assigned as the case owner.
